title.narrative: Accelerating Ecuador's Climate Change Initiatives with Strategic Action Plans and Investment Framew

description.narrative: The proposed Readiness grant envisions a comprehensive, well-structured approach to address this barrier informed by the identification and mapping of capacity gaps (Activity 1.3.1a and 1.3.1b). Resulting capacity needs will be cross-referenced against priority climate strategies and relevant stakeholders’ roles and responsibilities to inform the development of training programs (Activity 1.3.1c) targeting the 5 sectors of Ecuador’s PLANMICC. Having built the capacity of key stakeholders (Output 1.3.1), the proposed Readiness will enable the government of Ecuador to map out each step required to transform the PLANMICC mitigation vision into a granular action plan (Output 2.2.6) and supporting investment plan (Output 4.1.2) for the energy, agriculture, industrial processes, LULUCF and waste sectors. The Action Plan and Investment Plan will be complemented by a Stakeholder Engagement Strategy (2.2.6f) – including specific actions and targets for the involvement of women and vulnerable groups and objective prioritization methodologies (Activity 4.1.2b) resulting in enhanced stakeholder ownership and involvement in the implementation of the PLANMICC Action Plan (Output 2.2.6) and Investment Plan (Output 4.1.2) for 5 sectors, converting the nebulous concept of 'climate change mitigation objectives' into well-defined, actionable, and budgeted tasks guiding the implementation of the PLANMICC and NDC targets, thus addressing the lack of finance, detailed action and investment plans guiding the implementation of PLANMICC (barrier 2) and bankable climate change projects pipeline (barrier 3).

This Readiness proposal aims to contribute to cohesive climate change mitigation measures taken by country’s climate actors to effectively address climate change impacts through an enhancement of stakeholder coordination mechanisms and climate change thematic related knowledge, better harmonized policy frameworks from an inclusive and gender lens, and better access to climate finance.
